template: On the Grafana dashboard '{{v1}}' (at /d/{{v3}}/...), set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m'. Do this via the refresh picker in the top bar: open the refresh interval dropdown (next to the refresh button) and select '1m' from the Auto refresh / interval options. Then, to PERSIST this into the saved dashboard, open the dashboard settings (gear > Dashboard settings), go to the General settings, and set the 'Auto refresh' / 'Refresh interval' dropdown to '1m' if such a setting exists there, then Save. If the settings page has no such option, instead enter edit mode, click 'Save dashboard', and in the save dialog make sure any 'Update default time range' style option is handled so the refresh interval persists, then confirm the save. Report: the refresh interval shown in the top bar after saving, how you persisted it, and whether the save succeeded.

reportTemplate.summary: Set the dashboard auto-refresh to 1m using the top-bar refresh picker (it showed "Off"; picked the "1 minute" option). The dashboard settings General pane has no default-refresh dropdown — its "Auto refresh" control is a text field listing which intervals are offered (already containing 1m), so I used the fallback path: entered edit mode, clicked "Save dashboard", and in the save drawer ticked the checkbox "Update default refresh value" (please note the drawer's wording here is "Update default refresh value", not 'Update default time range'), which enabled the Save button, then confirmed the save and got the "Dashboard saved" alert. After saving I reloaded the dashboard from a clean URL with no ?refresh parameter and the top-bar picker still reads "1m" (aria-label "current interval 1 minute selected"), confirming the refresh interval persisted into the saved dashboard. Both panels are intact.
